To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a DNA‐85B vaccine‐induced protection against MTB infection is lost after boosting with Ag85B protein and that this loss is associated to an overwhelming Ag85B‐reactive CD4+ Th1 response, despite restraint of this response by CD8‐dependent mechanisms and CD4+‐dependent IL‐ 10 secretion.
the protein‐boosting of a DNA vaccine encoding the Ag85B protein may turn a protective response into a non‐protective one in mice, due to a massive expansion of Ag85B‐responsive CD4+ T lymphocytes.

Ag85B‐protein boosting of a DNA‐primed protective immune response against tuberculosis is associated to the loss of protection due to the induction of non‐protecting CD4+ Th1 cells, and that the Ag85B‐dependent expansion of these cells is associated to an impairment of their ability to produce IFNg and control intracellular MTB growth, and to an increase in IL‐10 production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the mechanisms that lead to the loss of protection induced by DNA‐priming and protein‐boosting vaccination against MTB.
the development of a novel tuberculosis vaccine.
the development of new vaccines for tuberculosis, which are based on a better understanding of the immune mechanisms that determine the instability of protective immune responses in this disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Ag85B protein‐dependent expansion and activation of non‐protectively CD4+ T responses, which is restrained by CD8+ and CD4+ T‐cell‐dependent IL‐‐10 production, could determine the instability of the protective anti‐tubercolosis immune response.
DNA‐priming and protein‐boosting schedules are not the most appropriate to develop an efficient MTB vaccine.
the Ag85B‐protein booster of a DNA‐85B‐induced Ag85B‐protective immune response in mice is not protective, but it is not harmful either.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ag85B‐protein‐dependent expansion of CD4+ cells is a key event for the loss of Ag85B‐induced protection.

Ag85B‐protein can induce an overwhelming CD4+ response that is non‐protective against MTB infection, and that Ag85B could contribute to the loss of protection induced by a DNA‐85B primary vaccination.
the Ag85B‐dependent loss of protection is associated with a massive Ag85B‐reactive T cell response, but that this massive Ag85B response is not sufficient to induce disease progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a protective Ag85B immune response may turn into a potent but ineffective Th1 immune response.
a protective anti‐tubercolous immune response may be lost by an excessive and/or uncontrolled Th1 immune response.
the Ag85B‐based vaccines, despite being the most studied, are not the best choice for a TB vaccine.
